title: Guardrails: layered validation and least privilege
objectives: Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects guardrails: layered validation and least privilege with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. The safe assistant can read fixtures and propose changes; actual writes require a matching unexpired action approval.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Guardrails are controls applied at specific boundaries: input validation, retrieval authorization, tool permissioning, output validation and rate limits. Moderation can classify content risks but cannot replace authentication or domain policy. Least privilege gives each component only the operations and data it requires.

Allowlisting provides a positive set of supported actions. Deny lists can supplement it for known attacks but are brittle as the primary permission mechanism. Human confirmation should approve a concrete action with scope and effect, not a vague intent.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Validate input size and types, derive identity from authentication, filter evidence before retrieval, restrict tool arguments and validate returned domain objects. Sandbox code candidates with bounded resources and no production credentials. Record policy decisions separately from model decisions.

An approval record includes action hash, principal, resource, expiry and status. Before execution, verify that the action still matches the approved payload and current permissions. Rate limits and anomaly checks bound abuse and accidental loops.

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A user approves a draft patch and the agent later applies a different generated patch using the same approval flag. A tool allowlist includes a generic shell wrapper, effectively restoring unrestricted execution.

Test action mutation, expired approval, revoked access, oversized input and unknown tools. Review false positives by use case and ensure safe fallback or escalation is available when a guardrail blocks progress.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: The safe assistant can read fixtures and propose changes; actual writes require a matching unexpired action approval. This rule is enforced in application code and tested with denied-call fixtures.
Release evidence identifies every guardrail's boundary and failure mode. Layered controls reduce reliance on any one classifier and make regressions diagnosable with deterministic assertions.

takeaway: The safe assistant can read fixtures and propose changes; actual writes require a matching unexpired action approval.

title: Output handling: redaction, rendering and policy layers
objectives: Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects output handling: redaction, rendering and policy layers with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. The shared report generator uses escaped HTML from the same JSON artifact.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Model output is untrusted content. Returning JSON does not make embedded strings safe for HTML, logs, SQL or tools. Context-specific encoding prevents output from becoming executable markup, while authorization controls which facts or actions may be produced. Moderation is another classifier with false positives and false negatives.
A sensitive value may appear in logs or traces even when the final answer is redacted. Apply privacy rules across artifacts, not only the user-facing response.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Render text through React's escaped text nodes and sanitize generated SVG before insertion. Escape model/log text in HTML reports. Redact sensitive structured attributes recursively, and store permitted raw evidence only in a separate controlled location with retention rules.

Keep schema validation, domain evidence checks, content policy and output encoding separate. A moderation pass cannot authorize a cross-tenant read, and HTML escaping cannot make an unsupported factual claim correct.

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A report directly interpolates <script> from a synthetic failure log. A shallow redactor removes api_key at the top level but misses it inside provider.request.headers. A deny-list phrase check misses paraphrased injection.

Test nested structures, case-insensitive sensitive field names, malformed output and dangerous markup. Verify that allowed ordinary content still renders and that blocked content produces a visible controlled outcome.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: The shared report generator uses escaped HTML from the same JSON artifact. The diagram editor combines strict Mermaid settings with sanitized SVG. These are rendering controls, while tool and tenant policies enforce operational boundaries.

SDETs should identify which layer each test protects. Passing one layer's test is not evidence that another layer's policy holds; retain separate verdicts for privacy, rendering, authorization and semantic support.

mistake: A report directly interpolates <script> from a synthetic failure log. A shallow redactor removes api_key at the top level but misses it inside provider.request.headers. A deny-list phrase check misses paraphrased injection.
takeaway: The shared report generator uses escaped HTML from the same JSON artifact.
